key_insight: TiN grain boundaries largely retain their strength after Nd/Ce segregation, unlike bcc Fe, despite favorable segregation in both materials.
engineering_relevance: TiN coatings may mitigate fuel-cladding chemical interaction damage by resisting grain-boundary weakening rather than excluding lanthanide fission products.
method: First-principles calculations for Nd/Ce segregation at six coincident-site lattice grain boundaries in each material.
Work-of-separation and traction-separation calculations to quantify ideal cleavage resistance.
Bonding analysis comparing replacement bonds in Fe with the surrounding Ti–N network.
evidence_signal: Median work-of-separation retentions for Nd/Ce were 1.00/0.97 in TiN versus 0.72/0.65 in Fe; peak-traction retentions were 0.85/0.85 versus 0.47/0.43.
watch_item: Ideal atomistic cleavage calculations do not directly establish coating performance under irradiation, finite-temperature corrosion, or real microstructural defects.
paper_title: Grain boundary strength and corrosion cracking susceptibility in TiN coatings under fission product segregation
